item.description:
# IPTVMac 0.25.37
- Trending Movies and Trending Shows now browse multiple TMDB pages and match them against the selected playlist locally. - Home preloads a useful window; open a Trending heading to browse the extended list. Scrolling prefetches more matches, with consecutive visible numbering. - One local catalogue index serves subsequent pages. Public feed pages are cached on the device, and already loaded cards survive a detail-page visit and return. - Failed page requests retain the loaded cards and offer Retry. - Movie and series details have a dedicated outline/filled Favorites heart. Favorites is removed from the detail + menu. - The detail ellipsis includes persistent Mark as Watched / Mark as Unwatched choices, separate from playback history and resume positions.
This version keeps the shared Apps Script TMDB service and the publisher's updated paging deployment. The separately discussed direct-TMDB/token-configuration proposal is not included. A title appears only when it can be matched to the selected provider; the number of playable results depends on that overlap. First-load network latency can still occur.
Validation: 142 selected native tests, two opt-in tests skipped, zero failures; 42 offline bridge tests passed. Separate-Mac update installation/relaunch has not been established by these local tests.
Apple Silicon (arm64), macOS 14 or newer. This is the owner's approved Apple Development-signed, unnotarized release; it is not Developer ID-signed or notarized. macOS may warn or block first launch. No security protection is disabled by the download helper.
No personal M3U/Xtream links, provider passwords, playlist databases or viewing history are included. Firebase public client configuration and service/update URLs are intentional. Application source remains in the private source repository.
IPTVMac-Runtime-Sources.zip contains the unchanged redistributable LGPL media runtime's exact sources, build recipes, patches, checksums and notices. Third-party notices are also included in the application.
